headline: 39 posts published before any Binance account spoke went on to reach 100K engagements each
dek: The first hour had a clear order: automated transfer alerts, a 39.5K-follower on-chain account naming it a hack, aggregators attaching numbers, and a Tether freeze headline. Binance-linked accounts spoke last.

key_numbers.label: Pre-statement posts that reached 100K by the cut

narrative: On-chain watchers broke the story, aggregators packaged it, and a stablecoin freeze hit the feed before Binance said anything. In the sampled posts, 39 published before the first Binance-linked post at 21:15 UTC, 51 minutes after the sweep, each passed 100K engagements by the cut, 13.8M together. None came from an official account: 18 were mid-size accounts (50K to 500K followers), 9 news aggregators, 8 small accounts and 4 large ones.

The machine signal came first and did not travel. Whale Alert's bot posted transfers out of #Binance from 20:23, including, per its own figures, 7,636 BTC at 20:30 and 780,000,000 USDC at 20:42. Each drew 40K to 90K engagements. At 20:32 (+8 minutes) @spreekaway, an on-chain account with 39.5K followers, wrote "Unconfirmed" and "Entire Binance wallet drained into new EOA", with a funding detail attached. It drew 1.6M engagements, about 40 per follower.

From +15 to +34 minutes, aggregators and mid-size accounts turned the alert into a number. @bwenews, @rektober and @crypto_banter repeated a reported "$2.53B in 60+ tokens"; @DarkWebInformer posted "$2.77 Billion" at +30 and @officer_secret "around $3.5B" at +32. At +18, @ASVPXILLZ said their own account had been compromised with about $3M withdrawn, an unverified individual claim, and drew 664K, more than any aggregator post in that window.
The first pushback came at +25 from @KillaXBT ("It's just fud", 238K). The first mechanism thread came at +30 from @odysseas_eth, an 8.7K-follower account whose EIP-7702 explanation drew 218K.

The freeze reached the feed before the company did. At 21:05 (+41), @TreeNewsFeed posted that Tether had frozen $971M USDT "WITH NO UPDATE FROM BINANCE STILL": 2.0M engagements, the largest post before Binance's first statement. @DeItaone (21:06) and @WatcherGuru (21:08, "No official statement from Binance yet", 605K) followed. At 21:15 @cz_binance quoted the TreeNewsFeed post and drew 3.2M, the biggest single post of the event; @binance's first statement in the same minute drew 95K.

By posting time, sampled posts published before CZ's earned 32 percent of the 55.4M engagements on all 686 sampled event-window posts; posts from the first 60 minutes earned 43 percent. The framing (hack, multi-billion figure, issuer freeze, company silence) was set before the first Binance voice appeared.

callouts.title: The 51-minute gap became the headline
callouts.body: 39 posts published before any Binance-linked account spoke passed 100K engagements each. The first institutional fact the crowd received was Tether's freeze, packaged with "no update from Binance". The silence was written into the most-engaged pre-statement post (2.0M).

callouts.title: Interpretation traveled, raw alerts did not
callouts.body: Whale Alert's automated transfer posts were early and drew 40K to 90K engagements each. A 39.5K-follower account calling it a possible hack drew 1.6M. Small on-chain accounts with high engagements per follower were the earliest layer that moved attention.

watch: Binance's post-mortem: whether it confirms or corrects the first-hour EIP-7702 framing, and whether the correction approaches 1.6M engagements.
More unverified user claims like @ASVPXILLZ's would shift the story from a hot wallet loss to account security.
The "EIP7702" keyword (1 to 27 posts in 24 hours): growth means the vector story is spreading to other wallets.
